title: Commitment Request Gating, Onboarding, and Backfill Protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a formalized intake, gating, and approval workflow for committed throughput requests that balances predictable SLAs with fleet safety and cost controls. This ticket covers: the intake form changes, an automated pre-screen scoring heuristic, human approval lanes and delegation, a short probation/backfill window after provisioning, and automated handoff artifacts for ops (autoscale templates, canary plan, rollback triggers). The goal is reducing manual triage time, preventing overcommit during high utilization, and giving customers a clear predictable onboarding path for reserved throughput.
acceptance_criteria: New intake form deployed (Confluence + web UI link updated) that captures workload profile, jitter/latency tolerance, 99th percentile SLO target, expected request concurrency, and budget band.
Automated scoring service returns one of: auto-approve, needs-sales-review, needs-ops-review, or deny, with rationale and numerical score. Thresholds documented.
Approval matrix implemented: delegated approvals for < X qps and < $Y/mo; PM+Ops signoff required for medium; Legal/Security loop for PII/high-compliance requests.
Provisioning playbook generated automatically (canary pool size, autoscale policy, KV cache warmup plan, rollback criteria) and attached to the request.
Backfill/probation period policy implemented: 7-day probation with utilization telemetry; automatic scale-back if customer underutilizes or violates rate profiles.
Cost estimate and committed-throughput SLAs surfaced to customer in onboarding email and in console reservation details.
Telemetry dashboard shows intake->approval->provisioning time for at least the last 30 requests and is accessible to PM/Ops.
Runbook links (GitHub PR + playbook) present in request record for oncall handover.
decision_log: 2025-02-20: Decided to use a numerical scoring heuristic instead of binary gating to reduce manual work; thresholds will be conservative for first quarter.
2025-02-24: Agreed on delegated approval limits: auto-approve if < 500 qps and estimated monthly cost < $10k; otherwise route to Ops queue.
2025-02-28: Chose 7-day probation window (vs 14) to reduce customer friction while still giving ops enough telemetry to validate traffic patterns.
2025-03-03: Opted to include a mandatory canary pool of 1–3 GPUs for first 24 hours for all requests flagged as "needs-ops-review".
2025-03-04: Decided to surface both committed throughput and cheap fallback bands to customers (e.g., committed with best-effort burst) in the console UI.
